Never use `--auto-deploy`.

rules/cli-reference.mdc.from: | `--ci` | Program-level flag, accepted anywhere on the line. Prompts go through `safePrompt` (`src/utils/prompt-handler.ts`), which under `--ci` throws `Interactive prompt required but --ci flag is set. Provide all required flags or arguments.` → **exit 1** — that is what `lua devices <action>` without `--device-name`, `lua devices test` / `test-trigger` on lua-cli 3.44 and older (they always prompt for the command / trigger name; ⏳ 3.45.0 takes `--command` / `--trigger` — devices.md §4), `lua governance`, `lua skills production` and `lua persona sandbox` do; they do **not** hang. `lua version create` (no `-m`) and `lua version delete` (no `--force`) **skip** their prompts under `--ci`: create proceeds with an empty message, delete proceeds **unconfirmed** (`src/commands/version.ts` ~58-61, ~439-450). A few commands still call `inquirer.prompt` directly and bypass the `--ci` guard: bare `lua env`, `lua pull` without `--force`, `lua auth logout` / `lua auth key` without `--force`, `lua chat` without `-m`/`-e`, and `lua test skill` without `--name` (its tool picker). On a TTY those block; with no TTY — Codex's Bash — inquirer hits EOF, the CLI prints the menu and **exits 0 having done nothing** (`src/utils/cli.ts` `ExitPromptError` → `process.exit(0)`): a false success, so never trust the exit code of a command that may have prompted. Always pass complete flags |

rules/cli-reference.mdc.from:
| ⏳ 3.38.0 `lua drains [list\|status\|deliveries\|create\|update\|delete\|test\|verify\|pause\|resume\|rotate-secret] [id] [--org <id>] [--json]` | **log drains** — copies the ORGANIZATION's agent log records to a destination it owns (`http` · `otlp` · `datadog` · `betterstack`). An org resource, so no project directory is needed: `--org`, else `lua.skill.yaml`, else the credential when it reaches exactly one org (several → exit 2 listing the ids). Needs **`logs:manage`**, a SENSITIVE scope a wildcard does not satisfy (missing → exit 10, one line, no `💡` block); reading the records themselves is `logs:read`. ⚠ `status` exits **2** when ANY drain is `failing` — the same code as a usage error, set AFTER printing, so decide from `drains[].state` in `--json`. `test`/`verify` are 202-then-poll (30 s / 60 s; `pending: true` and exit 1 when nothing landed — not a failure to send). Secrets are never flags: `--header <NAME>` prompts hidden, `--header-from-env <NAME>=<ENV_VAR>` is the `--ci` form, and the HMAC signing secret is minted server-side and printed exactly once (create, and `rotate-secret` without `--finalize`). Under `--json` stdout is the machine's and the verification/acknowledgement chrome goes to stderr. Every verb answers 404 → exit 3 until the org is enabled. Full reference: `lib/knowledge/log-drains.md`; the slash is `/lua-drains`. ⏳ **lua-cli 3.44.0** adds six destination types (`splunk`, `loki`, `axiom`, `newrelic`, `sumologic`, and `s3` for S3/R2/GCS buckets via `--provider`, `--bucket`, `--region`, `--prefix`, `--credentials-from-env KEY_ID_VAR=SECRET_VAR` or `--role-arn`/`--external-id`) and two verbs: `confirm <id> --token <t>` (settles a write-only bucket's ownership challenge) and `replay <id> <batchId>` (re-enqueues a refused batch inside the 6 h horizon); both sit in `ask`. `/lua-drains` still drives the four original types; use the CLI's `--help` for the others | RO for `list`/`status`/`deliveries`/`test`; **S** for the others (org config, `ask` tier — not a `P` deploy verb) |
| ⏳ 3.48.0 `lua decisions [list\|versions <name>\|run <name>\|publish <name> <version>\|delete <name>] [--json] [--force] [--state <json> \| --message <text>] [--provider jev\|openai\|openrouter\|auto] [--model <id>] [--min-confidence <n>]` | **named decisions** (`LuaDecision`) on the project's AGENT: `list` (default; aliases `ls`/`view`) shows each active decision with its current version and source; `versions` (`history`/`list-versions`) lists versions newest first with questions, provider and `minConfidence`, and also finds a deleted decision; `run` (`try`/`test`) runs the CURRENT version on `--message` (sent as `{ message }`) or `--state` (any JSON; both → exit 2, an empty message → exit 2) and prints one line per answer then provider, rule, model, duration, tokens, fallback — `--provider`/`--model`/`--min-confidence` override the version for that call only, and ⏳ **3.49.2** a `vendor/model` id such as `liquid/d1` runs on OpenRouter (`--provider openrouter` without `--model` is exit 2; a `typesafe/…` or `openai/…` id with it is refused naming the provider to use); `publish` (`rollback`/`deploy`) makes that version current at once, prints `old → new` with the questions added/removed, asks unless `--force`/`--ci`, and on a deleted decision turns it back on (409 → exit 10 when another decision took the name); `delete` (`rm`/`remove`/`del`) deactivates and keeps the versions (asks; `--force` required in CI, else exit 2). A failed `run` prints the decision error's own message: a 503 (`decision_timeout`/`decision_unavailable`/`decision_disabled`) exits 11, `decision_rejected` (422) is the model refusing the request itself and never falls back. `lua push decision --name <n>` stages a version (first push writes 1.0.1); it goes live with `lua version promote` or `publish`. `lua version status` shows live vs pinned vs yaml per decision. Rows: `lua logs --type decisions`. Full reference: `lib/knowledge/decisions.md`; the slash is `/lua-decisions`, scaffolding is `/lua-new decision` | RO for `list`/`versions`/`run` (a run is one billed call, 0.005 actions on Jev, 0.01 otherwise); **S** for `publish`/`delete` (agent config, `ask` tier — not a `P` deploy verb) |
| ⏳ 3.49.0 `lua browser read <url> [--selector <css>] [--format text\|html] [--wait-for <load\|networkidle\|css>] [-e sandbox\|production] [--agent-id <id>] [--json]` · `lua browser run "<task>" [--start-url <url>] [--schema <file.json>] [--max-steps <n>] [--max-cost <usd>] [--login <name>]… [-e] [--agent-id <id>] [--json]` | the agent's **cloud browser** from the terminal, on the platform, under the agent's **pushed** browser policy (engine, fallback, `allowedDomains`, `confirmActions`, `logContent`) — local code reaches it only after `lua push browser` + `lua push agent`. Needs `browser: true` or at least one named browser, else 409 `BROWSER_DISABLED`; the key needs `agents:write` on the agent (403). `read` opens one page in a new session, waits for `--wait-for`, prints title, final URL, engine, the HTTP status when it is not 200, `Matches:` for a `--selector`, `Blocked:`/`Guidance:` on a sign-in or bot wall, then the content (60 s). `run` prints `step N: <action> on <url>` as each step arrives, then status, steps, cost, engine, final URL and output, and `Waiting for confirmation:` when an action in `confirmActions` is held; `--max-steps` is 1–60 (default 25) and `--max-cost` 0.01–10 USD (default 1). ⏳ **3.57.0** `--login <name>` signs the run in with one of **your own** saved logins first, repeatable up to 5 (a code or a check pauses the run and emails you a private link; ⏳ **3.58.0** adds the files and page-script settings a browser may carry). A run has 5 minutes, the CLI stops waiting after 6 and exits 1, and `Ctrl-C` cancels it **on the server** (exit 130). `-e` only TAGS the log rows (`dev` channel) — the browser, policy and cost are identical. ⚠ `--json` prints the raw envelope (`{ engine, data, error?, code? }` / `{ id, status, result }`) and **exits 0 even when the call failed**: read `error`/`code`, never the exit code. At most **2** CLI reads and runs at once per agent (429 `BROWSER_CLI_CONCURRENCY`; a slot frees itself within 6 min), paused limiter 503 `BROWSER_CLI_LIMITER_UNAVAILABLE`. ⏳ **3.49.2** checks `-e`, `--format`, the caps, the URLs, an empty task, the `--schema` file and the `--login` names locally (exit 2) before anything is sent. Rows: `lua logs --type browser`. Full reference: `lib/knowledge/browser.md`; the slash is `/lua-browser`, scaffolding is `/lua-new browser` | RO for `read` (one session, no model calls, nothing changed); **S/P-shaped** for `run` — it acts on a real third-party site and spends model budget, so it sits in the `ask` tier (not a `P` deploy verb: no Lua state changes) |

rules/devices.mdc.from: - **Without `--out` the secret is printed once to stdout.** In Codex that is the conversation transcript, so the plugin **always** passes `--out` — the `block-device-secret` hook blocks the command otherwise — and never `cat`s, `source`s, `grep`s, `head`s or echoes the file. Never pass `--force` unless the user asked to replace the file.

Never pass `--force` unless the user asked to replace the file.

rules/integrations.mdc.from: Then the only custom code is (a) a `LuaWebhook` or `defineTrigger` that reacts to the subscribed events and (b) tools for derived logic (e.g. `find_optimal_meeting_slot`). Do not call any." -t mcp-discovery-1` and let the agent recite its surface.

rules/web-apps.mdc.from: - **The plugin's use:** it is safe to run — nothing goes live and nothing is sent — so after `lua push webapp` the plugin may offer it and, when the user wants to click through, run it and hand over the link. It is in no permission list, so Codex asks once before it runs. Never present a preview as "deployed": only `/lua-deploy webapp` makes a version live.
